Definition: from G575 and G4762; to turn away or back (literally or figuratively):--bring again, pervert, turn away (from).
BiblicalUsage: To turn away or turn back covers a wide road. Jesus says do not turn away from the one who would borrow from you, He tells Peter to put his sword back in its place, Paul says the Deliverer will turn ungodliness away from Jacob, and he warns that some will turn their ears away from the truth toward fables.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe turning is the hinge of the whole Bible. Turn away from a needy neighbour and you have turned from Christ; turn away from the truth and you have turned toward a story of your own making.
